mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 3% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY growth > 3% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the unemployment rate increase does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real estate activity (HOUST) over three months signals a weakening demand in the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the decline in HOUST does not correlate with broader economic demand indicators.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over two months signals strengthening economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the increase in INDPRO does not correlate with broader economic supply indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or the decrease in FEDFUNDS does not correlate with subsequent easing actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 5% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decline for two consecutive months, it signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% and PAYEMS declines for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with broader economic weakness indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative for two consecutive quarters and retail sales (RSAFS) decline by more than 2% over the same period, it signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 negative growth for 2 quarters and RSAFS declines > 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint condition does not correlate with broader recessionary indicators.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, when the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals a restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the increase in FEDFUNDS does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.
